relations.definition: Indicates the starting point or origin of an action or movement.
relations.embedding_query_text: from: Indicates the starting point or origin of an action or movement.

instances: Swift left Thursday night's event -> Madison Square Garden

chosen_property.label: fromLocation
chosen_property.justification: The 'fromLocation' property is a good fit for indicating the starting point or origin of a movement.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: announcementLocation
candidates.comment: An announcement location relation between a special announcement and the specific civic structure or local business it pertains to. Also called relevant location, associated place, specific venue. Examples: "A special announcement's announcement location is 'City Hall'.", "The emergency announcement's announcement location is 'Local Grocery Store'." Distinct from spatialCoverage, which is used for larger geographic regions.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: area
candidates.comment: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."

candidates.label: startTime
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning time of an action, reservation, or media segment. Also called "beginning time", "commencement time", "start of action", "reservation time". Examples: "The reservation has startTime 7:00 PM", "The action's startTime was 10:30 AM", "The media clip's startTime is 00:01:15.". Distinct from startDate, which specifies a date, while startTime focuses on the time of day or an offset.

candidates.label: areaServed
candidates.comment: An area served relation between a contact point, offer, organization, or service and the geographic region where it is available. Also called service area, coverage region, delivery zone. Examples: "A restaurant's area served is 'Downtown'.", "The delivery service's area served is 'California'.", "An organization's area served is 'Worldwide'."

candidates.label: foundingLocation
candidates.comment: A founding location relation between an organization and the place where it was established. Also called: place of origin, establishment location, birthplace. Examples: "Microsoft" founding location "Albuquerque, New Mexico", "Apple Inc." founding location "Los Altos, California", "Google" founding location "Menlo Park, California".

candidates.label: availableAtOrFrom
candidates.comment: A place from which an offer can be obtained. Also called: pickup location, sales point, distribution point. Examples: "Offer 'Groceries' availableAtOrFrom 'Supermarket A'", "Offer 'Concert Tickets' availableAtOrFrom 'Venue Box Office'."

candidates.label: startOffset
candidates.comment: A temporal offset indicating the start time of a clip or action, measured in seconds from the beginning of a larger work. Also called "clip start time", "beginning offset", "time offset start", "seek start". Examples: "The video clip has startOffset 30 seconds", "The action's startOffset is 120 seconds into the recording", "This segment begins at startOffset 0."

candidates.label: birthPlace
candidates.comment: A place where a person was born. Also called: place of birth, birthplace. Examples: "Person 'Albert Einstein' birthPlace 'Ulm, Germany'", "Person 'Marie Curie' birthPlace 'Warsaw, Poland'."

relations.definition: Specifies the date or time of arrival at home.
relations.embedding_query_text: arrived home on: Specifies the date or time of arrival at home.

instances: Swift left Thursday night's event -> early hours of Friday morning

chosen_property.label: arrivalTime
chosen_property.justification: The 'arrivalTime' property is the best fit for specifying the date or time of arrival.

candidates.label: arrivalTime
candidates.comment: An expected time of arrival for a trip. Also called: estimated arrival, scheduled arrival, landing time. Examples: "Trip to NYC arrivalTime '2023-10-27T14:30:00'", "Flight 789 arrivalTime '18:00'", "Bus Trip arrivalTime 'tomorrow 09:15'."

candidates.label: dateReceived
candidates.comment: A temporal arrival relation between a message and the date/time it was received by the recipient. Also called: reception date, message arrival time, delivery time. Examples: "Email" date received "2023-10-26T10:25:00Z", "Package Notification" date received "2023-10-26T11:00:00Z". Distinct from dateSent, which is when the message was dispatched.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: availableFrom
candidates.comment: A date and time when an item is available for pickup from a store or locker. Also called: pickup start time, ready for collection. Examples: "DeliveryEvent 'Package' availableFrom '2023-10-27T10:00:00'", "DeliveryEvent 'Order' availableFrom '2023-10-28'". Distinct from availableThrough, which specifies the end of pickup availability.

relations.definition: Indicates the educational institution a person attends.
relations.embedding_query_text: is student at: Indicates the educational institution a person attends.

instances: Elizabeth Maxey -> University of Mississippi
Hayden Mason -> University of Mississippi

chosen_property.label: affiliation
chosen_property.justification: The 'affiliation' property is the best fit for indicating a person's association with an organization, including being a student.

candidates.label: alumniOf
candidates.comment: An alumni of relation between a person and an educational organization or organization they are a former student or member of. Also called graduated from, formerly attended, past affiliation. Examples: "A person is alumni of 'MIT'.", "John Doe is alumni of 'Boy Scouts of America'." Distinct from alumni, which describes the inverse relationship (organization to person).

candidates.label: alumni
candidates.comment: An alumni relation between an educational organization or organization and a person who is a former student or member. Also called former student, graduate, past member. Examples: "A university's alumni include 'Jane Doe'.", "The club's alumni include 'John Smith'." Distinct from alumniOf, which describes the inverse relationship (person to organization).

candidates.label: affiliation
candidates.comment: An affiliation relation between a person and an organization they are associated with. Also called associated with, member of, works for, belongs to. Examples: "A professor's affiliation is 'Harvard University'.", "A player's affiliation is 'Local Soccer Club'." Distinct from alumniOf, which specifies a past association with an educational organization.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: brand
candidates.comment: A brand or organization associated with a product, service, or maintained by an organization or person. Also called: product brand, service brand, corporate brand. Examples: "Product 'Smartphone' brand 'Apple'", "Service 'Cloud Storage' brand 'Google'", "Organization 'Company X' brand 'Brand Y'."

candidates.label: termsPerYear
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating how many terms of study are offered per year within an educational or occupational program. Also called "terms offered annually", "semesters per year", "academic terms per year". Examples: "The program has termsPerYear 2", "The educational program's termsPerYear is 4 (quarters)", "This institution offers termsPerYear 3 (trimesters)."

candidates.label: funder
candidates.comment: A funder relation between a creative work, event, grant, organization, or person and the organization or person providing financial support or sponsorship. Also called: sponsor, benefactor, financial supporter. Examples: "Art Exhibition" funder "National Endowment for the Arts", "Research Project" funder "NIH", "Charity Event" funder "Local Bank". Distinct from fundedItem, which is the item receiving funding.

candidates.label: educationRequirements
candidates.comment: An education requirements relation between a job posting or occupation and the educational credentials or text describing the necessary background. Also called "required education", "educational qualifications", "academic prerequisites". Examples: "Job posting 'Software Engineer' educationRequirements 'Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science'", "Occupation 'Doctor' educationRequirements 'MD'", "Job 'Teacher' educationRequirements 'Teaching Credential'".

candidates.label: memberOf
candidates.comment: A membership relation between an organization or person and the organization or program membership they belong to. Also called: belongs to, is a member of, affiliated with. Examples: "John Doe memberOf 'Local Sports Club'", "Acme Corp memberOf 'Industry Association'", "Jane Smith memberOf 'Premium Membership Tier'". Distinct from member, which expresses the inverse relationship.
